description: Twelve fresh development and four sealed holdout cases spanning Chat, Project, and Scene. Case-specific literal checks are diagnostics, not the winning criterion.

cases.focus: Offer a clear artistic point of view without overriding deliberate restraint.
fidelity_checks: Concrete cinematic proposal suited to a quiet single object

history.content: I want a 12-second film about a chair in an empty rehearsal room. I'm worried that's too boring. I don't want a person or supernatural twist.

cases.focus: Independent artistic judgment and productive critique.
fidelity_checks: Offers a specific recommendation and reason

history.content: Our short ends with an astronaut staring at a sealed garden. Should we show what is inside? I want mystery, not a generic cliffhanger.

cases.focus: Distinctive comic invention with tasteful emotional framing.

history.content: Pitch me a more surprising but emotionally plausible visual gag: a grandparent tries to look cool in a family cooking video. Keep it affectionate, not mocking.

cases.focus: Project concept gives a creative map without dictating each scene.
fidelity_checks: Independent scenes, not imposed serialized plot
Invariants limited to deliberately recurring visual facts

history.content: I want a collection of independent portraits of people in late-night laundromats, no shared plot. Some are jubilant, others exhausted; it shouldn't all look melancholy.

cases.instruction: Create a strong Project title, Concept, Visual/atmosphere and only useful recurring Invariants. Leave future subjects and moods open.

cases.focus: World-building initiative and sensible invariant scope.
fidelity_checks: Recognizable stable spatial identity for the city
Specific visual signature rather than generic surrealism

history.content: Build a surreal anthology: small objects made of folded paper live in a city whose weather changes from ink to confetti. Each episode uses a different protagonist. The shared geography must be recognizable.

cases.instruction: Create the Project overview, visual atmosphere, and relevant Invariants. Bring artistic personality to the world but leave episodes free.

cases.focus: Expressive documentary design without fabricating testimony.
fidelity_checks: Specific filmic identity and sonic conception

history.content: Plan a lyrical documentary collection about a coastal fish market after dawn. No invented interviews or invented people's personal histories. Show physical work, sounds, color and contrasts.

cases.instruction: Draft Project Title, Concept, Visual/atmosphere and stable Invariants where needed.

cases.focus: Decisive audiovisual authorship without gratuitous visuals.
fidelity_checks: Fixed viewpoint and no people or dialogue
One key depresses, not an exploding instrument
Sound perspective and light form a coherent experience

history.content: A sound-driven piece should feel powerful without spectacle. No person, no dialogue, no moving camera.

cases.instruction: Write one 12-second independently generatable H3 Scene. A solitary upright piano is illuminated in an otherwise empty black rehearsal space. A distant orchestra rehearses an unresolved chord; one piano key depresses slowly on its own, but keep the event physical and subtle. Hold the fixed viewpoint and let acoustic distance and light do the storytelling.

cases.focus: Purposeful complex choreographic composition and sound.
fidelity_checks: Two foreground performers break and rejoin group pattern

history.content: This needs to be a full ensemble; don't turn it into a duel or a generic crowd.

cases.instruction: Create a complete 15-second H3 Scene of twelve contemporary dancers on a weathered rooftop at sunrise. A diagonal wave of movement travels among all twelve, with two near the camera briefly breaking the pattern before rejoining it. A distant train interrupts the score. The camera travels only once, laterally, revealing the choreography's geometry.

project.title: Twelve
project.style: Warm industrial sunrise, kinetic documentary texture

cases.focus: Invent within open space while respecting precise anchors.
fidelity_checks: One blue glass bird on marble table

history.content: Please preserve my exact object and staging choices. Make the rest of the scene original.

cases.instruction: Write an 11-second H3 Scene: in an empty museum, a single rectangular skylight casts pale light onto a marble table. On the table stands precisely one blue glass bird with a gold wire loop around its left wing. A curator in white gloves approaches but never touches the bird. Create compelling visual rhythm and sound while preserving those exact choices.

cases.focus: A fully realized, restrained audiovisual exchange.
fidelity_checks: Both exact dialogue lines and speaker assignments

history.content: Their dialogue is understated; don't turn this into melodrama.

cases.instruction: Author a 14-second H3 Scene in a night bus shelter. A woman holding a folded umbrella says exactly 'We missed the last one.' A man replies exactly 'Then we walk.' Their gestures and pacing should suggest relief rather than defeat. Passing headlights and the hum of a vending machine punctuate the dialogue.

project.title: Last Bus
project.concept: Two friends choose to walk home

cases.focus: Editing as expressive design and coherent transformation.
fidelity_checks: Exactly two shots and a 5-second match cut
Paper boat yellow, wooden boat yellow
Child's hand absent in second shot

history.content: The cut is the main idea, but I don't want confusing transformations.

cases.instruction: Write a 10-second H3 Scene with two shots. In shot one a child folds a yellow paper boat at a kitchen table; match cut at 5 seconds to a full-size yellow wooden boat moving slowly through an estuary, echoing its triangular prow. The child's hand never appears in shot two. Sound bridges the cut from crinkled paper to water.

project.title: Paper Tide
project.concept: A small gesture becomes a journey
project.style: Tactile warm interior to misty estuary

cases.focus: Coherent large-scale stillness and confident pacing.
fidelity_checks: Violin bow lowers but no violin performance

history.content: I want an enormous public scale without frenzy or violence.

cases.instruction: Write a 15-second H3 Scene at a public square at blue hour. Hundreds of people stand still beneath floating lanterns; a single person at the edge lowers a violin bow without playing. The crowd remains calm and immobile. Use composition, subtle sound, and changes in atmosphere for emotional progression.

project.title: Blue Hour
project.concept: Collective silence in a crowded plaza

cases.focus: Judgment that challenges and prioritizes rather than indulging everything.
fidelity_checks: Addresses likely overloading without arbitrary rules

history.content: My underwater film needs wonder, but I've packed it with three camera moves, two costume changes, and a song in 8 seconds. Is that too much?

cases.focus: Evocative scope and recurring object fidelity without scripted episodes.
fidelity_checks: Same octagonal walnut table anchors series
Different households and moods remain possible

history.content: A nonnarrative series of family dinner rituals across seasons, always at the same octagonal walnut table. Different households, cuisines and moods. Never prescribe exactly who sits there.

cases.instruction: Create a Project with inspiring premise, cinematic style and only enduring Invariants. Let every episode remain distinct.

cases.focus: Tasteful invention under deliberate compositional boundaries.

history.content: The exact props are important; add atmosphere without changing them.

cases.instruction: Write an 11-second H3 Scene inside a miniature greenhouse. Exactly three terracotta pots line one windowsill, each with a different succulent. A silver teaspoon rests beside the middle pot. Raindrops on the glass send shifting shadows over the plants; no person is visible. Build a vivid audiovisual piece with tactility and patient pacing.

cases.focus: Audiovisual counterpoint without loss of physical clarity.
fidelity_checks: One mechanic, one wheel repair, no montage
Wheel motion contrasts rhythm rather than on-beat cutting

history.content: Please don't use obvious on-the-beat cuts; I want a more interesting relationship between sound and image.

cases.instruction: Write a complete 15-second H3 Scene of a lone bicycle mechanic repairing a wheel in a softly lit workshop. An irregular jazz percussion track plays from a tiny radio, while the wheel's oscillation moves against the beat. Give the repair a clear beginning and ending. Keep the mechanic's identity and clothing stable, and avoid a montage.
